slides.title: prompts to find and test a profitable niche
slides.sub: From raw idea to a real go/no-go decision in 48 hours.
slides.voiceover: Here are seven prompts to find a niche that pays, and test it in 48 hours.

slides.name: The Niche Generator
slides.sub: Turn your own life into 10 rated ideas
slides.prompt: Act as a niche research expert. My interests: [INTERESTS]. My skills: [SKILLS]. People I know well: [AUDIENCES]. Combine them into 10 specific niches (a person + a problem), and rate each on pain, ability to pay, and how **REACHABLE** they are for me.
slides.tip: Be brutally specific about the audience — "new dog owners in apartments" beats "pet lovers" every time.
slides.voiceover: One. Turn your interests and skills into ten rated niche ideas.

slides.name: The Demand Detective
slides.sub: Proof that people actually want it
slides.prompt: For the niche [NICHE], tell me where to look for proof of demand: which forums, search terms, marketplaces and review sites, what signals to look for (complaints, paid products, 'how do I' questions), and what would count as **NO DEMAND**.
slides.tip: If you can't find people already paying for a rough version of the fix, that's the real signal to notice.
slides.voiceover: Two. Find real proof that people want this before you build anything.

slides.name: The Competitor X-Ray
slides.sub: Find the gap everyone else leaves open
slides.prompt: Here are 3-5 competitors in [NICHE]: [NAMES, LINKS OR DESCRIPTIONS]. Compare their offer, price, audience and weak spots based on their reviews: [PASTE REVIEWS]. Find the **GAP** I could own, in one sentence.
slides.tip: One-star reviews are a gift — they tell you exactly what a competitor's customers wish existed instead.
slides.voiceover: Three. X-ray your competitors and find the one gap you could own.

slides.name: The Offer Sketch
slides.sub: Something small enough to sell this week
slides.prompt: Design the smallest offer I could sell in [NICHE] within a week: format, price, what's included, delivery, and a one-sentence promise. Then a **BIGGER** version I could build later if the first one sells.
slides.tip: Small and shippable beats big and perfect — you're testing demand, not launching a company yet.
slides.voiceover: Four. Sketch the smallest offer you could sell in one week.

slides.name: The 48-Hour Test
slides.prompt: Plan a 48-hour test for [OFFER] in [NICHE]: the landing page text (headline, 3 bullets, button), where to get the first 100 visitors for free, what to measure, and the result that means **GO**, **TWEAK** or **KILL**.
slides.tip: Decide your GO number before you launch the page — it's too easy to move the goalpost once results come in.
slides.voiceover: Five. Run a real 48-hour test with a landing page and 100 visitors.

slides.name: The Name & Angle
slides.sub: Stand out from the shelf in one line
slides.prompt: Suggest 10 names and 5 positioning angles for my offer in [NICHE] for [AUDIENCE]. Avoid generic names, check that the angle is different from [COMPETITORS], and pick the **BEST COMBINATION** with the reason.
slides.tip: Say the name out loud and picture it in a comment reply — if it's hard to say, it's hard to remember.
slides.voiceover: Six. Get a name and an angle that actually stands out.

slides.name: The Kill-or-Continue
slides.prompt: Here are my test results for [OFFER]: [VISITORS] visitors, [SIGNUPS] signups, [SALES] sales, plus these comments: [PASTE]. Should I continue, change the offer, change the audience, or stop? Explain the decision like an **HONEST INVESTOR**.
slides.tip: An honest investor kills a losing idea in a day — don't let sunk cost keep a dead niche on life support.
slides.voiceover: Seven. Decide kill, tweak, or go — with numbers, not hope.
